match.reason: The only candidate is an accounting card on residual value in depreciation, which is a different idea from the residual (actual minus predicted) in regression, so no bank point teaches this point.

draft.title: Residuals and residual plots
card: A residual is the actual value minus the predicted value: residual = y − ŷ. The predicted value ŷ comes from the regression line.
A positive residual means the point is above the line, so the line predicted too low. A negative residual means the point is below the line.
A residual plot graphs the residuals against x. A plot with no clear pattern, with points scattered randomly about zero, supports a linear model.
A curve or other clear pattern in the residual plot shows a linear model is not suitable. Worked example: actual y = 40 and predicted ŷ = 46 gives a residual of 40 − 46 = −6.
draft.remember: Residual = actual − predicted. A random scatter supports a line.

a.q: A line predicts a plant height of 25 cm. The plant is actually 22 cm tall. What is the residual?
a.why: Residual = actual − predicted = 22 − 25 = −3 cm. The answer 3 cm reverses the subtraction, which is the tempting sign error.
a.clue: Actual comes first in the subtraction.

b.q: The residual plot for a linear model shows a clear U-shaped curve. What does this suggest?
opts: A linear model is not suitable
A linear model is a good fit
b.why: A clear pattern such as a curve means the line is missing structure in the data, so a linear model is not suitable. A good fit would show random scatter with no pattern.
b.clue: Which kind of residual plot supports a line?

b.best: A linear model is not suitable

final.title: Residuals and residual plots
card: A residual is the actual value minus the predicted value: residual \(= y - \hat{y}\). The predicted value \(\hat{y}\) comes from the regression line.
A positive residual means the point is above the line, so the line predicted too low. A negative residual means the point is below the line.
A residual plot graphs the residuals against \(x\). A plot with no clear pattern, with points scattered randomly about zero, supports a linear model.
A curve or other clear pattern in the residual plot shows a linear model is not suitable. Worked example: actual \(y = 40\) and predicted \(\hat{y} = 46\) gives a residual of \(40 - 46 = -6\).

2.alt: A regression line with two points marked. One point is above the line, with an arrow up from the line to it: a positive residual. The other is below the line, with an arrow down from the line to it: a negative residual.

final.remember: Residual \(=\) actual \(-\) predicted. A random scatter supports a line.

a.clue: Actual comes first in the subtraction.

opts: A linear model is not suitable

wants.brief: A residual plot, Residual on the vertical axis from -4 to 4 and x along the horizontal axis, with a bold zero line and 12 points scattered above and below it with no pattern.
wants.why: It shows the random scatter about zero that supports a linear model.
notes: The 12 residuals alternate exactly above, below, above, below from left to right, which is a regular pattern rather than the random scatter the card describes; mix the signs so some neighbours are on the same side of zero.
The residuals add to -0.7 rather than about 0, as residuals from a least squares line should; balance the points above and below the zero line.
